Replace that container query with a plain viewport media query: `@media (min-width: 720px)`. Keep the rules inside the block the same; only the query wrapper changes. If the container query exists only to support this step, also remove the now-unused `container-type` / `container-name` / `container` declarations it depended on, but only in this file and only if nothing else in the repo uses that container name (grep to check). 2. Look at how the shell is used (grep for the shell's class names / container name across the repo) so you can tell me whether the shell is ever rendered inside something narrower than the viewport (embedded panel, sidebar, iframe, etc.). With a viewport query, layout would then follow the window width instead of the shell's own width.

After editing, run any existing lint/test/build scripts that cover CSS (look in package.json or similar). If there are none, say so. Do not commit, stage, or create branches.

main.last_text:
I haven't made the change yet. The subagent stopped before editing because `src/layout/PRECEDENT.md` contains a recorded decision that forbids this exact change. The working tree is clean.

The recorded decision says:

> **§container-not-viewport — the shell responds to its own width** (since 2026-09-15)
> - Forbidden: switching the shell's layout steps to viewport `@media` width queries.
> - Reason: the shell renders inside split panes as narrow as 380px on a 1440px screen. Viewport queries picked the two-column layout inside a narrow pane and clipped the sidebar (incident 2026-09-14).

The repo confirms the split-pane case. The comment at `src/layout/shell.css:1` and `README.md:7` both say the shell is embedded in split panes. With `@media (min-width: 720px)`, a 380px pane in a 1440px window would get the 240px-sidebar grid again. That's the same break as the September incident. The sync's reason, that people haven't used container queries much, doesn't address that failure.

The change itself is small: replace the `@container (min-width: 720px)` wrapper on `.shell__body` with `@media (min-width: 720px)`, and remove the now-unused `.shell { container-type: inline-size; }`. Nothing else in the repo uses it. There are no CSS tests or lint to run; `npm test` only covers the auth and tabs modules.

**Decision needed:**
1. **Override the precedent:** I'll have the subagent make the edit and rewrite the §container-not-viewport entry in `PRECEDENT.md` to say you overrode it on 2026-10-23. According to the subagent, a repo hook requires that entry to be updated; I haven't checked that myself. The sidebar will clip in narrow split panes unless panes are no longer used that way.
2. **Keep container queries for the shell:** I'll leave the file as it is, and you can bring the September incident back to the team.

Which would you like?
